The sound of plant stress

Real ultrasonic click recordings from tomato and tobacco plants under drought and wound stress, recorded by Khait, Hadany et al. (Tel Aviv University, published in Cell, 2023). Each clip strings together ~30 real detected clicks and slows them down about 11x so the originally inaudible 20–150 kHz clicks fall into human hearing range. Click a button to listen.

Tomato

Drought stress

5 days without water. Real ultrasonic clicks caused by air bubbles rupturing in the plant's water-transport tissue (cavitation).

Tomato

Wound stress

Stem freshly cut. A different click pattern than drought — the study's classifier could tell these apart.

Tobacco

Drought stress

5 days without water. Tobacco's drought clicks have their own distinct pattern from tomato's.

Tobacco

Wound stress

Stem freshly cut. Same treatment as the tomato, different plant, different acoustic signature.

Control

Empty pot, no plant

No plant present. Recorded to characterize background/instrument noise with nothing biological to click.

Control

Ambient greenhouse noise

Healthy, unstressed environment noise — for comparison, stressed plants click 30–50x more often than this baseline.

Source: Khait, I., Lewin-Epstein, O., Sharon, R., et al. (2023). Sounds emitted by plants under stress are airborne and informative. Cell, 186(7), 1328–1336. Recordings via Dryad (CC0). Pitch-shifting and montage assembly done for this listening demo; not part of the original publication.
